newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower after stock disappointment.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower after stock disappointment.

text.p: COMEX copper ended lower after a dull session, the market failing to gain momentum following a less-than-expected dip in LME stocks on Tuesday.
LME stocks overall fell 2,525 tonnes to 121,175 tonnes, about half of what traders expected.
Stocks in Long Beach dipped 4,625 tonnes to 29,150 tonnes.
The rise in COMEX stocks appears to have slowed down, with much smaller tonnages going into warehouses in recent days. COMEX stocks were up 73 short tons Tuesday to 31,564 tons.
David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said until there are changes in supply or demand, the market will continue to oscillate around 90 cents.
"The focus will continue to be on LME stocks," Rinehimer said. Low stocks give support to the market below 90 cents, while the pending surplus in copper caps any rallies.
December COMEX settled 1.40 cents weaker at 92.05 cents per pound, traded 93.50 to 91.60 cents. Spot November went out 1.10 cents lower at 93.10 cents.
Volume was estimated at 8,000 lots, slightly above Monday's official 6,308 lots.
The market was also awaiting Wednesday's LME November options declaration.
